questions.question: Q: What is the difference between demographic and psychographic profiling?

points.text: Demographics classify audiences by objective, measurable characteristics — age, gender, income, occupation. Psychographics classify by subjective traits — values, attitudes, interests, and lifestyle. Demographics tell you WHO the audience is; psychographics tell you WHY they consume media and what motivates them.

questions.question: Q: How do media producers use audience profiling to target products?

points.text: Producers use demographic and psychographic data to identify target audiences, then design content and marketing to appeal to them. A teen horror film is marketed on TikTok with short clips and influencer partnerships (psychographic: thrill-seekers). A broadsheet newspaper is marketed through subscription offers to educated professionals (demographic: ABC1).

questions.question: Q: Evaluate the ethics of data-driven audience targeting.

points.text: Data-driven targeting enables more relevant content and advertising, improving user experience. However, it raises ethical concerns: data is often collected without meaningful consent, profiling can be intrusive, political micro-targeting can manipulate voters, and children may be targeted inappropriately. GDPR and ASA regulation provide some protection but enforcement is inconsistent.

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: Media products target specific audiences through deliberate choices of content, language, visual style, and distribution channels, informed by demographic and psychographic profiling. The target audience is identified through demographic and psychographic analysis. Demographics define who the audience is — age, gender, income, location. Psychographics define what motivates them — their values, interests, and lifestyle choices. Together, these profiles guide every production and marketing decision. Content is designed to appeal to the target audience's psychographic profile. If the audience values authenticity and social justice (Reformers), the product will feature realistic representations and progressive themes. If the audience values status and image (Aspirers), the product will feature aspirational lifestyles and success imagery. Visual codes further target the audience. Colour palettes, typography, and imagery are chosen to resonate with the target demographic — bright, bold colours for younger audiences; sophisticated, muted tones for affluent audiences. Distribution channels are selected based on where the target audience consumes media. Young audiences are reached through TikTok and Instagram; older audiences through television and newspapers. The platform choice itself targets the audience. Marketing language also reflects audience profiling.
